topic: Digital signals, codes and spread spectrum

questions.question: What is Quadrature Amplitude Modulation or QAM?

choices.A: A technique for digital data compression used in digital television which removes redundancy in the data by comparing bit amplitudes
choices.B: Transmission of data by modulating the amplitude of two carriers of the same frequency but 90 degrees out of phase
choices.C: A method of performing single sideband modulation by shifting the phase of the carrier and modulation components of the signal
choices.D: A technique for analog modulation of television video signals using phase modulation and compression

questions.answer: Transmission of data by modulating the amplitude of two carriers of the same frequency but 90 degrees out of phase

questions.question: What is the definition of symbol rate in a digital transmission?

choices.A: The number of control characters in a message packet
choices.B: The maximum rate at which the forward error correction code can make corrections
choices.C: The rate at which the waveform changes to convey information
choices.D: The number of characters carried per second by the station-to-station link

questions.answer: The rate at which the waveform changes to convey information

questions.question: Why should the phase of a PSK signal be changed at the zero crossing of the RF signal?

choices.C: To improve carrier suppression

questions.question: What technique minimizes the bandwidth of a PSK31 signal?

choices.C: Use of sinusoidal data pulses

questions.question: What is the approximate bandwidth of a 13-WPM International Morse Code transmission?

choices.C: 52 Hz

questions.question: What is the bandwidth of an FT8 signal?

choices.C: 600 Hz

questions.question: What is the bandwidth of a 4,800-Hz frequency shift, 9,600-baud ASCII FM transmission?

choices.C: 4.8 kHz

questions.question: How does ARQ accomplish error correction?

choices.A: Special binary codes provide automatic correction
choices.B: Special polynomial codes provide automatic correction
choices.C: If errors are detected, redundant data is substituted
choices.D: If errors are detected, a retransmission is requested

questions.answer: If errors are detected, a retransmission is requested

questions.question: Which digital code allows only one bit to change between sequential code values?

choices.B: Extended Binary Coded Decimal Interchange Code
choices.C: Extended ASCII

questions.question: How can data rate be increased without increasing bandwidth?

choices.C: Using a more efficient digital code

questions.answer: Using a more efficient digital code

questions.question: What is the relationship between symbol rate and baud?

choices.B: Baud is twice the symbol rate
choices.C: Baud rate is half the symbol rate
choices.D: The relationship depends on the specific code used

questions.question: What factors affect the bandwidth of a transmitted CW signal?

choices.C: Keying speed and shape factor (rise and fall time)

questions.answer: Keying speed and shape factor (rise and fall time)

questions.question: What is described by the constellation diagram of a QAM or QPSK signal?

choices.A: How many carriers may be present at the same time
choices.B: The possible phase and amplitude states for each symbol
choices.C: Frequency response of the signal stream
choices.D: The number of bits used for error correction in the protocol

questions.answer: The possible phase and amplitude states for each symbol

questions.question: What type of addresses do nodes have in a mesh network?

choices.C: Internet Protocol (IP)

questions.question: What technique do individual nodes use to form a mesh network?

choices.A: Forward error correction and Viterbi codes
choices.C: Discovery and link establishment protocols
choices.D: Custom code plugs for the local trunking systems

questions.question: Why are received spread spectrum signals resistant to interference?

choices.A: Signals not using the spread spectrum algorithm are suppressed in the receiver
choices.B: The high power used by a spread spectrum transmitter keeps its signal from being easily overpowered
choices.C: Built-in error correction codes minimize interference
choices.D: If the receiver detects interference, it will signal the transmitter to change frequencies

questions.answer: Signals not using the spread spectrum algorithm are suppressed in the receiver

questions.question: What spread spectrum communications technique uses a high-speed binary bit stream to shift the phase of an RF carrier?

choices.C: Binary phase-shift keying

questions.question: Which describes spread spectrum frequency hopping?

choices.A: If interference is detected by the receiver, it will signal the transmitter to change frequencies
choices.B: RF signals are clipped to generate a wide band of harmonics which provides redundancy to correct errors
choices.C: A binary bit stream is used to shift the phase of an RF carrier very rapidly in a pseudorandom sequence
choices.D: Rapidly varying the frequency of a transmitted signal according to a pseudorandom sequence

questions.answer: Rapidly varying the frequency of a transmitted signal according to a pseudorandom sequence

questions.question: What is the primary effect of extremely short rise or fall time on a CW signal?

choices.C: The generation of key clicks

questions.question: What is the most common method of reducing key clicks?

choices.A: Increase keying waveform rise and fall times
choices.B: Insert low-pass filters at the transmitter output
choices.C: Reduce keying waveform rise and fall times
choices.D: Insert high-pass filters at the transmitter output

questions.answer: Increase keying waveform rise and fall times

questions.question: What is the advantage of including parity bits in ASCII characters?

choices.C: A larger character set is available
choices.D: Some types of errors can be detected

questions.answer: Some types of errors can be detected

questions.question: What is a common cause of overmodulation of AFSK signals?

choices.C: Bit errors in the modem

questions.question: What parameter evaluates distortion of an AFSK signal caused by excessive input audio levels?

choices.C: Repeat Request Rate (RRR)

questions.question: What is considered an acceptable maximum IMD level for an idling PSK signal?

choices.C: +15 dB

questions.question: What are some of the differences between the Baudot digital code and ASCII?

choices.A: Baudot uses 4 data bits per character, ASCII uses 7 or 8; Baudot uses 1 character as a letters/figures shift code, ASCII has no letters/figures code
choices.B: Baudot uses 5 data bits per character, ASCII uses 7 or 8; Baudot uses 2 characters as letters/figures shift codes, ASCII has no letters/figures shift code
choices.C: Baudot uses 6 data bits per character, ASCII uses 7 or 8; Baudot has no letters/figures shift code, ASCII uses 2 letters/figures shift codes
choices.D: Baudot uses 7 data bits per character, ASCII uses 8; Baudot has no letters/figures shift code, ASCII uses 2 letters/figures shift codes

questions.answer: Baudot uses 5 data bits per character, ASCII uses 7 or 8; Baudot uses 2 characters as letters/figures shift codes, ASCII has no letters/figures shift code

questions.question: What is one advantage of using ASCII code for data communications?

choices.A: It includes built-in error correction features
choices.B: It contains fewer information bits per character than any other code
choices.C: It is possible to transmit both uppercase and lowercase text
choices.D: It uses one character as a shift code to send numeric and special characters

questions.answer: It is possible to transmit both uppercase and lowercase text
